title: Staged Rollback Runner for Offline Batching & Cache Simulation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a 'staged rollback runner' that performs offline, policy-aware dry-run simulations of batching and KV-cache configuration changes for Private/VPC deployments, produces deterministic apply recipes, and supports safe staged rollback when policies or metrics violate SLO/cost constraints. This is an automation component for the cost-optimization pipeline that must operate without contacting customer production endpoints (offline mode), respect VPC/KMS policies, and emit artifacts that operators can review before any live apply.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can ingest a proposed config change (batch size, cache TTL, cache key schema, quantization profile) and run a dry-run simulation against historical traces stored in the customer's telemetry export (S3/Drive) without contacting live services.

Dry-run output includes: estimated per-token savings, expected p50/p95 tail latency delta, KV cache hit-rate delta, and a risk score computed against configured policy rules (latency SLO, customer-defined unsafe models, KMS-access constraints).
If the policy engine flags a high-risk result, the runner generates a staged rollback recipe (sequence of revert-steps) and marks the change as 'requires manual approval'.

Artifacts (diff, simulation report, staged-rollback recipe, signatures) are written to the project's secure storage path and an operator-facing checklist is created in the Console rollout UI for review.
End-to-end e2e tests that run the runner in CI using synthetic VPC telemetry must pass and block merges if regressions are detected.
technical_design: Architecture: The runner is a containerized service that executes three phases: 1) Transform: normalize incoming config delta and generate candidate parametrizations; 2) Simulate: run a deterministic simulator over historical traces (prefix-aware KV cache model + batching queuing model + kernel-selection performance table) to produce metrics; 3) Evaluate & Emit: feed metrics into the policy evaluator to compute pass/fail and generate staged-rollback recipes. Offline constraints: the service must not open outbound connections to customer endpoints; KMS policy checks are performed against policy descriptors (IAM/KMS metadata) provided in the config bundle. Data model: reports are JSON blobs containing flat fields (token_cost_savings_estimate, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, cache_hit_delta, risk_score, policy_violations).
implementation_plan: Week 1: Build simulator core and adapter for archived telemetry (S3/Drive manifest parser).
Week 2: Implement policy evaluator DSL capable of expressing: latency SLOs, disallowed models, min_cache_hit thresholds, KMS key usage constraints.
Week 3: Add staged-rollback recipe generator that maps simulation failures to a minimal revert sequence and optional throttled rollback (canary-style).
Week 4: Integrate with Console artifacts writer and add operator checklist + dry-run approval flow (no autopublish).
Week 5: Add CI e2e suite and runbook; security review and penetration test for storing dry-run artifacts (encrypted at rest).
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only runner that runs against sandbox VPC traces; UI link in Console under 'Optimize -> Dry Runs'.
Beta: allow opt-in for selected customers with signed config bundles; require security approval and support on-call during first runs.
GA: enable runner for Dedicated/Private customers as a Console action, defaulting to 'dry-run + manual approval' mode; autopublish disabled for 6 months.
test_plan: Unit tests for simulator modules (cache model, queuing model, kernel perf table).
Integration tests using synthetic traces that mimic large seq length variance to exercise batching heuristics.
Policy fuzz tests: random config deltas with randomized policy descriptors to verify staged-rollback recipe correctness.
Load tests: run simulator in parallel across 50 candidate configs to validate resource usage and execution time (goal < 15m per bundle).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Simulator divergence from live performance due to unseen kernel scheduling effects. Mitigation: include calibration step that compares simulator predictions with small shadow runs and store calibration factors per-hardware-profile.
Risk: Sensitive metadata leakage in dry-run artifacts. Mitigation: encrypt artifacts with customer KMS key descriptors and redact PII; require security review before customer opt-in.

Risk: Operators misinterpret risk scores and approve unsafe changes. Mitigation: provide human-readable rationale and top-3 contributing policy violations in report; require two-approver flow for high-risk changes.

Risk: Offline mode misses dynamic runtime behaviors (autoscaling interactions). Mitigation: flag config deltas that touch autoscaling and mark them as 'no offline guarantee' requiring a canary live test.
design_decisions: Do not enable automatic live-apply in Private/VPC for GA — all applies require manual approval for at least one release cycle.
The staged rollback artifact is a linear sequence of idempotent API calls (config set/unset) rather than attempting to compute inverse config transforms to keep revert semantics simple.
Policy evaluation DSL will be intentionally conservative; any unknown policy predicate will evaluate to 'violation' to favor safety.
